name: Princeton
description: Flat-rate handyman repairs for Princeton homes, from the older houses off Nassau Street to Riverside, Littlebrook, and the Western Section.
localContext: Princeton has some of the oldest housing in central New Jersey, and it shows on the repair list. In-town houses near Nassau Street and in the Western Section still have plaster walls, original wood doors that have swelled and settled for a century, and casing profiles no big-box store carries. Riverside and Littlebrook are largely 1950s and 60s ranches and split-levels, which means hollow-core doors, original tile with tired grout, and decks that are on their second or third owner. Our work here is the small stuff done carefully: plaster patched as plaster, doors planed rather than replaced when they are worth keeping, fixtures swapped like-for-like with no permit. Princeton is a straight run down Route 1 from our Middlesex County shop and one of the towns we are in most weeks.

name: West Windsor
description: Flat-rate handyman repairs for West Windsor homes around Princeton Junction, Dutch Neck, Grovers Mill, and Penns Neck.
localContext: Most of West Windsor was built in a single burst between the late 1980s and the early 2000s, so the colonials off Village Road, Southfield Road, and Clarksville Road are all hitting the same milestones at the same time: builder-grade interior doors that never quite closed, the first round of faucets and light fixtures giving out, decks that need boards and a coat of stain, and drywall that has settled around the window corners. That is Half Day territory. Many homeowners here commute from Princeton Junction, so we confirm by text, send an on-the-way message, and can work from arranged access for standing clients. West Windsor is about ten minutes off Route 1 for us.

name: Plainsboro
description: Flat-rate handyman repairs for Plainsboro townhomes and single-family homes, from Princeton Collection and Ravens Crest to Plainsboro Village.
localContext: Plainsboro is townhome and condo country: Princeton Collection, Ravens Crest, Hunters Glen, Fox Run, and the rest of the communities along Plainsboro Road and Scudders Mill Road went up between the late 1970s and the 1990s. Inside those units the list is predictable and we know it well: bifold closet doors off their tracks, dated bath fixtures, caulk that has failed around tubs, ceiling fans that wobble, and TVs that need to go on a party wall properly. Exterior work in the associations is usually the HOA's job, so we keep to the inside unless the association says otherwise. Plainsboro sits right off Route 1 near Forrestal Village, which makes it one of the easiest towns for us to fit into a same-week slot.

name: Lawrence Township
description: Flat-rate handyman repairs for Lawrence Township, from Lawrenceville village to Eldridge Park, Slackwood, and the neighborhoods off Princeton Pike.
localContext: Lawrence Township runs the length of Route 1 and Route 206 between Princeton and Trenton, and the houses change by the mile: prewar colonials and Victorians in Lawrenceville village, 1950s capes and ranches in Eldridge Park and Slackwood, and 1980s and 90s colonials and townhomes off Princeton Pike and Franklin Corner Road. The older streets give us plaster repairs, doors that have shifted with the house, and original wood windows that need weatherstripping. The newer ones give us the standard 30-year list: fixtures, doors, deck boards, and grout. Either way it is one flat price agreed before we start. Lawrence is an easy Route 1 run for us.

name: Montgomery
description: Flat-rate handyman repairs for Montgomery Township homes in Skillman, Belle Mead, and Blawenburg.
localContext: Montgomery Township is large-lot living along Route 206 and Route 518: colonials from the 1990s and 2000s subdivisions in Skillman and Belle Mead, older farmhouses and capes around Blawenburg, and a lot of decks, sheds, and exterior trim exposed to weather with nothing to block the wind. The newer houses have heavy millwork and built-ins that need matching when a piece is damaged, plus the usual first-round replacements of fixtures and doors. Many properties are on well and septic, which does not change our work but does mean we confirm shutoff locations before touching a faucet. Montgomery is just north of Princeton for us, up 206 from the Route 1 corridor.

name: Pennington
description: Flat-rate handyman repairs for Pennington Borough and the surrounding Hopewell Township streets that share the 08534 ZIP.
localContext: Pennington is a small borough with a Main Street of Victorians and Colonial Revivals, ringed by 1960s through 1990s neighborhoods like Brookside and the Hopewell Township streets that share the ZIP. The borough houses give us the careful jobs: casing and stair parts worth repairing rather than replacing, plaster cracks, and old doors tuned rather than tossed. The newer streets give us decks, fences, fixtures, and drywall. We stay on the repair side of the line here; exterior changes in the historic district are the borough's call, and we do not do renovations anyway. Pennington is out Route 31 for us, past Princeton, and we book it like every other town: one price, agreed before we start.

name: South Brunswick
description: Flat-rate handyman repairs for South Brunswick homes in Kendall Park, Monmouth Junction, Dayton, and Kingston.
localContext: South Brunswick covers a lot of ground between Route 1 and Route 27, and the housing runs from the 1950s and 60s ranches and split-levels of Kendall Park to the 1990s and 2000s subdivisions in Dayton and Monmouth Junction. Kendall Park is where we see the original hollow-core doors, first-generation bath tile with failing grout, and trim that has been painted so many times the profile is gone. Dayton and Monmouth Junction are the 25-year list: builder fixtures, decks due for boards and stain, and drywall cracks at the window corners. South Brunswick sits between our Middlesex County base and Princeton, so it is on the way to almost everything we do down here.

name: Cranbury
description: Flat-rate handyman repairs for Cranbury, from the historic village on Main Street to the homes along Cranbury Neck Road and Old Trenton Road.
localContext: Cranbury is a small township with a well-kept historic village along Main Street and Maplewood Avenue, and larger properties on the roads running out toward Cranbury Neck and Old Trenton Road. The village houses are 18th and 19th century in places, which means plaster, wide old casing, doors that have settled for generations, and the kind of small repairs that need patience more than power tools. We repair what is there rather than replacing it wholesale, and we stay inside the repair line: exterior changes in the historic district are for the township's preservation commission and a contractor who does that work. Cranbury is a short hop off Route 130 for us.

name: East Windsor
description: Flat-rate handyman repairs for East Windsor homes, including the Twin Rivers townhomes and the neighborhoods around Hightstown.
localContext: East Windsor is best known for Twin Rivers, one of the first planned unit developments in the country, where thousands of townhomes went up in the early 1970s. Fifty years on, the inside of those units is our bread and butter: doors that have never hung square, bath fixtures on their last legs, caulk and grout gone black, and drywall patched a few times by previous owners. The single-family streets in Hickory Acres and Princeton Manor are 1960s to 1990s colonials and capes with the usual list of decks, fences, doors, and fixtures. East Windsor is on Route 130 and Route 33 for us, an easy run from the Turnpike side.

name: Robbinsville
description: Flat-rate handyman repairs for Robbinsville homes in Town Center, Foxmoor, Washington Town Center, and the surrounding subdivisions.
localContext: Robbinsville is one of the newer towns we work in: most of the housing went up from the 1990s through the 2010s, with Town Center and Washington Town Center adding walkable townhomes and condos along Route 33. Newer does not mean nothing breaks, it means the builder-grade parts fail on a schedule: door hardware, faucets, disposals, ceiling fans, deck boards, and gate hinges all reach the end of their first life around the fifteen-year mark. Townhome associations here usually cover the exterior, so most of our Robbinsville visits are inside work and TV mounts. Robbinsville is out Route 130 and Route 33 for us, at the southern edge of where we go.
